title: The Blind Man and the Honored Pages

paragraphs.text: This surah begins with a gentle lesson given to the Prophet himself. The ayahs say that he frowned and turned away, because a blind man came to him and interrupted him. Then the Prophet is asked a question that makes him reflect: how could he know that this man might be purified, or that he might be reminded and benefit from the reminder? The passage then compares two kinds of people. On one side is the person who thinks he needs nothing, and to him the Prophet was giving his attention, even though it would not be his fault if that person refused to be purified. On the other side is the man who came eagerly, striving for knowledge while he feared Allah, and yet the Prophet was distracted from him. Through this comparison, the ayahs teach that a sincere heart which seeks guidance deserves care and attention, whatever his situation may be. The lesson is told openly and honestly, and it shows how carefully the Quran guides the way people should be treated.

Then comes a firm "No!" which marks a change of direction. These verses are a reminder, and anyone who wishes may remember them and take benefit from them. They are recorded in honored sheets, which are exalted and kept pure. They are carried by the hands of messenger-angels who are noble and dutiful. These descriptions show how precious and protected the message is. It is not ordinary speech, but something carefully preserved from its source until it reaches people. For this reason, a reader should approach it with respect and with a willing heart.

The passage ends this section with a strong statement about human beings. Man is cursed, and how great is his disbelief! After hearing about such a noble reminder, carried in such a respected way, many people still refuse to believe. This short ayah expresses amazement at how ungrateful and stubborn a person can be when the truth is placed right in front of him. It also prepares the reader for the next part of the surah, which will remind man of where he came from and of the many blessings he has been given. In this way, the ayahs move from a personal lesson to a lesson for all of humanity.
